note: DSE Toolkit tools for the HQ Tools page. The runner only runs these; it never sends, posts or pays.

dse.daily.label: My engine: next send lists
dse.daily.help: Builds the engine's next dated send lists: finds new leads (or checks your seed websites), checks what each one is missing, drops anyone already on your lists, picks each lead's channel within your daily caps, and drafts the opener in your wording. They appear in the Send Desk.

fields.name: per_day
fields.label: Leads per day (empty = the engine's setting)

dse.list.label: Leads + problem check (the daily one)
dse.list.help: Finds independent businesses of one type near your cities, keeps those with a live website, checks what each site is missing for your path, and writes a ready opener per lead. Run 'Download business data' for that type once first. Spot-check, then Add to my CRM.

choices.label: AI Automation (back-office work done by hand)

dse.podcasts.label: Podcast leads (Broadcast Engine)
dse.podcasts.help: Active business podcasts from Apple Podcasts' free search, with what each show is missing (gaps between episodes, no video, thin show notes) and the host's public email when the feed lists it.

dse.check.label: Problem check on a list
dse.check.help: Checks every website in one of your lists for what your path sells, adds the gaps and an opener per row.

choices.label: AI Automation (back-office work done by hand)

dse.check_one.label: Problem check on one website
dse.check_one.help: One website, results in the log. Good for a parish you know, a shop from the Meta Ad Library, or a lead someone referred.

choices.label: AI Automation (back-office work done by hand)

dse.find.label: Leads only (no check)
dse.find.help: Just the lead list: independent businesses of one type with a live website.

dse.mystery_new.label: CareBridge: start a mystery-shop tracker
dse.mystery_new.help: Turns a home-care lead list into a tracker. You send each enquiry yourself, then fill in when you sent it and when they replied.

dse.mystery_score.label: CareBridge: score agencies by reply time
dse.mystery_score.help: Hot = no reply after 48 h or a reply after 24 h+; Warm = 1-24 h; Cold = within the hour. Reach out to Hot and Warm only.

dse.build.label: Download business data (once per type)
dse.build.help: Downloads one or more business types from Foursquare's free open data (needs your free Hugging Face token set on the PC; README). Do it once, then monthly.

howto.ask.label: How to do it (your path's tools)
howto.ask.help: Step-by-step recipes written from the tools' official help pages: Clay, Apollo, HubSpot, Sales Navigator, Instantly, Lemlist, n8n, Vapi, Cal.com, GoHighLevel, Klaviyo, Descript, CapCut, LinkedIn posts, sales calls and the whole GTM system. Each recipe gives the goal, what to have ready, steps with why each matters and what you should see, mistakes to avoid, a 'you are done when' check, the official source links and the date it was checked. Ask in your own words, like: enrich my list with emails in clay. Menus and plans change: if a button differs, open the source link in the answer.

fields.name: question
fields.label: What do you want to do?

chat.ask.label: HQ chat: ask anything
chat.ask.help: Ask anything about selling, discovery calls, objections, cold messages, follow-ups, pricing and proposals, freelancing, international clients, planning, focus, decisions, rejection, writing, or any tool in the stack. Answers are grounded in HQ's researched guides and recipes. Three levels, best available is used: (1) Claude, the strongest: set your own Claude API key as the Windows user variable ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, run pip install anthropic, and restart the runner (your question and the matching guide text go to Anthropic, you pay your own usage; nothing else is sent unless you ask about your progress). (2) Free local AI with Ollama: install it from ollama.com, run ollama pull gemma3:4b (about 3.3 GB, needs about 8 GB RAM, also reads pictures), set OLLAMA_MODEL=gemma3:4b and restart the runner. gemma3:1b works on small PCs but gives thinner answers. (3) With neither, you get the matching researched guide or recipe in full. The answer says which one wrote it. To ask about a picture in Citadel, use DBI-AI with an image-capable model.

fields.name: question
fields.label: Your question (up to 2000 characters)
fields.placeholder: a client says it is too expensive

app.build.label: App Builder: build any website or app
app.build.help: Builds a real, working project for you: a website, web app (installs on phones), native phone app (iPhone + Android), desktop app (Windows/Mac) or TV app (Samsung, LG, Android TV). Pick a starting point (landing page, dashboard, store, booking), your name, colour and one line about it. You get a folder in builds/ with the app, a README with the exact commands to run and publish it, a BUILD-BRIEF of what to build next, and rules so an AI coding agent can carry on. Needs Node.js LTS (nodejs.org) for everything except the plain website. Tick 'Install and test the build' to have it prove the app builds (a few minutes). Nothing is published or paid for: you deploy yourself.

choices.label: Web app (installs on phones, works offline)
Landing page: home, pricing, about, contact

fields.label: One line: what it does and who it is for

fields.label: Contact email for forms (website only, optional)

yt.plan.label: YouTube Launchpad: plan my channel
yt.plan.help: Builds your whole YouTube channel plan from zero: your niche and promise, channel name ideas, setup checklist, the exact Partner Program (monetisation) numbers and what they mean in views, a faceless-safe policy guide, tools that cost nothing, a 13-week roadmap matched to your weekly hours, a weekly routine, and 30 video ideas with titles, hooks, thumbnail briefs and Shorts. Works faceless or on camera. Read CHANNEL-PLAN.md first. It teaches the method and the honest odds: it cannot promise income.

fields.label: Hours per week you can give

yt.ideas.label: YouTube Launchpad: more video ideas
yt.ideas.help: Adds more video ideas to your channel's ideas.csv: titles that fit one window, a hook, a thumbnail brief and a Short for each. Give an angle (something you know well) and it puts a video on that first.

yt.script.label: YouTube Launchpad: write a video script
yt.script.help: Turns a video idea into a ready-to-record script plan: hook options, promise, sections with timing, on-screen cues, call to action, five title options, the thumbnail brief, description and pinned comment, a Short cut-down and a pre-upload checklist. Tick the AI box for a first draft from your own free Ollama (rewrite it in your voice: original content is what YouTube rewards).

fields.name: ai
fields.label: Add an AI first draft (needs Ollama, takes a few minutes)

yt.track.label: YouTube Launchpad: weekly numbers and progress
yt.track.help: Type this week's numbers from YouTube Studio (subscribers, watch hours in the last 12 months, Shorts views in the last 90 days, and if you can the click-through rate and average percentage viewed). It shows how far you are from the Partner Program numbers, your weekly pace, and the three things to fix next. Do it once a week.

yt.check.label: YouTube Launchpad: check a title and thumbnail
yt.check.help: Checks a video's packaging before you publish: title length and keyword position, shouting and clickbait wording, thumbnail words, and the first lines of the description. Gives a score and exact fixes.

dse.followups.label: My engine: plan follow-ups
dse.followups.help: Finds everyone you messaged (and marked Sent) who has not answered, works out who is due for a second or third message, drafts it and saves it as a list in the Send Desk. Rules: touch 2 and 3 come due 3 and 7 days after an email or Instagram message (Facebook 4 and 9, website form 5 and 12), Sundays are skipped, there is never a second Instagram DM (a comment, then a note by email or form), and it stops when they reply, book, are lost or you skip. Only rows you marked Sent count; it lists any you never marked. You still send every message yourself.

dse.outcomes.label: My engine: results
dse.outcomes.help: What the engine is really producing, from the taps you made in the Send Desk: messages sent, replies, calls booked, clients won and the monthly value, by channel, by the gap you led with, by wording and by touch. It only calls a difference when both sides have 30 or more sends in the same channel, and it tells you which first messages were never marked Sent or Skipped.

dse.import_check.label: My engine: check my file
dse.import_check.help: Go-to-Market and Authority engines build their lists from a file YOU make. Go-to-Market: a CSV exported from your own Clay, Apollo or HubSpot account, saved in engines/<engine>/imports/ on your PC. Authority: a CSV of experts you looked at and pasted by hand (name, profile_url, headline, connections, post_dates, post_1, post_2), saved in engines/<engine>/pasted/. This shows which columns were understood, how many rows, and the best prospects, so a wrong column shows up before you build a list. Nothing is scraped from LinkedIn or anywhere else.

ascent.callscore.label: The Ascent: score a sales call
ascent.callscore.help: After every sales call, real or a mock you recorded, rate it honestly in eight areas (0 missed, 1 partly, 2 done well). You get your score, the two weakest areas with a 10-minute drill each, and your numbers over time: show rate, close rate, cash per call, what you earned in commission, and your score trend. Be harsh: a scorecard that flatters you teaches nothing. Based on the up-front contract, SPIN-style questions and the pause-ask-answer objection routine (HQ recipe: Prepare and run a high-ticket sales call).

fields.label: How much of the call did YOU talk (%)

fields.name: a4

fields.name: a8
fields.label: 8. Asked for the decision and followed up

dse.calls.label: The Ascent: my call history
dse.calls.help: Your logged calls and totals: how many, how many sold, cash, and your average score.

ascent.vet.label: The Ascent: vet a commission offer
ascent.vet.help: Before you give a high-ticket, commission-only offer your time, answer the questions (Yes, No or Not asked yet). You get a verdict (Walk away, Red, Amber, Unchecked, OK or Promising), the exact reasons, a ready message with the questions to put to them in writing, what to get in the contract, and what one sale and a target month would really need from you. Based on the FTC's job-scam advice (never pay for a job, earnings promises, fake checks, unverifiable employers) and practitioner guidance for commission contracts. It informs your decision; it is not legal advice. It saves the offer to your tracker.

fields.name: ticket
fields.label: Price of the offer they sell ($)

fields.name: target
fields.label: Monthly income you want from it ($)

fields.name: d_pay
fields.label: DEALBREAKER: Do they ask you to pay anything to start: training, certification, starter kit, deposit, leads or software?

fields.name: d_contract
fields.label: DEALBREAKER: Do they refuse to put the commission terms in writing before you start?

fields.name: d_earnings
fields.label: DEALBREAKER: Did they promise or hint at what you will earn to get you to join (for example 'our closers make $20k a month', guaranteed income)?

fields.name: d_money
fields.label: DEALBREAKER: Do they ask you to receive money, cash a check, forward payments, or buy gift cards?

fields.name: d_hidden
fields.label: DEALBREAKER: Is the company impossible to verify: no named owner, no registered business, or a website or contact that does not work?

fields.name: s_rate
fields.label: SERIOUS: Is the commission rate, or what it is calculated on (cash collected or contract value), unclear?

fields.name: s_payout
fields.label: SERIOUS: Is the payout later than 30 days after the client pays, or is no payout date stated?

fields.name: s_clawback
fields.label: SERIOUS: Can they take your commission back (refunds, chargebacks) with no written time window or cap?

fields.name: s_proof
fields.label: SERIOUS: Can you not verify real customers or results (no named customers, no reviews outside their own pages)?

fields.name: s_regulated
fields.label: SERIOUS: Is the offer in a regulated area (credit repair, lending, trading, investing, insurance) where selling may need a licence?

fields.name: s_leads
fields.label: SERIOUS: Will you be cold-calling your own leads, with no stated source or number of booked calls?

fields.name: s_exclusive
fields.label: SERIOUS: Do they want exclusivity or a non-compete without a guaranteed base or minimum?

fields.name: s_control
fields.label: SERIOUS: Are you called a contractor but told your hours, must follow a script you cannot change, and cannot work for others?

fields.name: s_nobody
fields.label: SERIOUS: Do they refuse to let you speak to a current closer or the person you would report to?

fields.name: c_payment
fields.label: CAUTION: Is there no clear way to be paid internationally (for example Wise, Payoneer or bank transfer), or unclear who pays the fees?

fields.name: c_pressure
fields.label: CAUTION: Do they pressure you to decide fast ('spots are filling', 'offer ends today')?

fields.name: c_recordings
fields.label: CAUTION: Are your calls recorded without being told how the recordings are used or who owns them?

fields.name: c_nda
fields.label: CAUTION: Is the NDA or ownership clause broader than the job (for example it stops you working in the industry afterwards)?

fields.name: c_refund_rate
fields.label: CAUTION: Do they refuse to say their refund or chargeback rate?

fields.name: p_contract
fields.label: GOOD SIGN: Did they send a written agreement draft showing rate, base, payout date and clawback terms?

fields.name: p_named
fields.label: GOOD SIGN: Can you name the founder and find the company in a business registry (US state registry or UK Companies House)?

fields.name: p_closer
fields.label: GOOD SIGN: Did you speak to a current closer who confirmed pay and lead flow?

fields.name: p_inbound
fields.label: GOOD SIGN: Do they supply warm leads (calls booked from their own content or ads)?

fields.name: p_reviews
fields.label: GOOD SIGN: Do independent customers or reviews outside their own pages confirm the product works?

fields.name: p_data
fields.label: GOOD SIGN: Will you see your own call data and results (CRM or recordings) so you can prove your numbers?

dse.offers.label: The Ascent: my offer tracker
dse.offers.help: Every offer you vetted, best verdict first, with its status, price and commission.

dev.config.label: Dev: what is allowed on this PC
dev.config.help: Shows what the dev tools may do here (editing, tasks, pushing to GitHub, PowerShell). These switches can only be changed at the PC itself, never from here.

dev.workspaces.label: Dev: my workspaces
dev.workspaces.help: Lists your workspaces (project folders on this PC), what kind of project each is and which git branch it is on.

dev.new.label: Dev: start a new project
dev.new.help: Creates a project folder with starter code, a test and git, in one of 14 starters: JavaScript, TypeScript, Python (command line or web API), Java, Kotlin, C#, C, C++, Dart, Flutter, Go, Rust, PowerShell. Tick the last box to use the language's own generator when it is installed.

fields.name: official
fields.label: Use the language's own generator if installed

dev.clone.label: Dev: copy a GitHub repository here
dev.clone.help: Copies a repository from GitHub into a workspace so you can read and change it. Public repositories need no login; private ones use the GitHub login on this PC.

dev.repo.label: Dev: look at a GitHub repository
dev.repo.help: Reads a repository's description, language, stars and default branch from GitHub.

dev.issues.label: Dev: open issues of a GitHub repository
dev.issues.help: Lists the latest open issues and pull requests.

dev.tree.label: Dev: show the files
dev.tree.help: Lists the files and folders of a workspace.

dev.read.label: Dev: read a file
dev.read.help: Shows a file with line numbers. Files that hold secrets (.env, keys) are never shown.

fields.name: path
fields.label: File path inside the workspace (like src/app.py)

dev.search.label: Dev: search the code
dev.search.help: Finds lines matching a word or pattern in every file of the workspace.

dev.replace.label: Dev: change a line of code
dev.replace.help: Replaces text in a file. The old text must match exactly once. For bigger changes use Dev: let the AI make a change.

fields.name: path
fields.label: File path inside the workspace (like src/app.py)

dev.run.label: Dev: install, build, test or lint
dev.run.help: Runs the project's own install, build, test or lint step (npm, pip, Maven, Gradle, dotnet, CMake, Dart, Flutter, Cargo, Go). If a tool is missing it tells you the one command that installs it.

dev.status.label: Dev: what changed (git status)
dev.status.help: Shows the branch and which files changed.

dev.diff.label: Dev: show the changes (git diff)
dev.diff.help: Shows exactly what changed since the last commit.

dev.branch.label: Dev: start a branch
dev.branch.help: Creates and switches to a new git branch.

dev.commit.label: Dev: save a commit
dev.commit.help: Saves the current changes as a commit. Refuses if a file that looks like a secret would be included.

dev.pull.label: Dev: update from GitHub (pull)
dev.pull.help: Brings in new commits from GitHub (fast-forward only, it can never rewrite your work).

dev.push.label: Dev: push to GitHub
dev.push.help: Pushes the current branch to GitHub. Works only when you switched pushing on at this PC and the repository belongs to an account you allowed. From main it pushes a new dev/ branch instead; it never forces.

dev.pr.label: Dev: open a pull request
dev.pr.help: Opens a pull request on GitHub for the current branch (same permission as pushing, and your GitHub login on this PC).

dev.agent.label: Dev: let the AI make a change
dev.agent.help: An AI engineer reads the project, edits the files, runs the tests and saves the result on a NEW branch (dev/agent-...). It cannot leave the workspace, read secrets, run a shell or push. You read the diff, then push yourself. Uses Claude when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set on this PC, otherwise your local Ollama model.

fields.name: instruction
fields.label: What should change? (one or two sentences)

dev.shell.label: Dev: run a PowerShell command
dev.shell.help: Runs one PowerShell command inside a workspace. OFF unless you turned it on at this PC (allow_shell). Dangerous commands are refused, but this is not a sandbox: switch it on only if you accept that.
